title: Can grazers persist in this pond?
caption: Your question becomes an inspectable experiment.
notes: Name organisms and who eats whom.
Roles and feeding links are separate settings.
hint: Start with a simple food web.

title: Choose the conditions.
caption: Choose the conditions you want to explore.
notes: Resources supply energy for life.
Supported pressures shape the starting conditions.
hint: Change one thing you can explain.

title: Give the experiment a direction.
caption: What would you like to investigate?
notes: A preference guides supported strategies.
It does not guarantee the outcome.

title: Check the world before it begins.
caption: Review the actual settings, then play.
notes: Check roles, links and founder estimates.
You choose when to seed the world.

title: Learn to read the habitat.
caption: Birth, feeding and death cues mark recorded events.
notes: Species colors distinguish populations.
Green marks show resources; warm marks show hazard.
hint: Pause when a change catches your attention.

title: Turn one creature into a closer look.
caption: Inspection pauses the world.
notes: Read energy, age and living family.
Keep the selected subject beside the habitat.
hint: Zoom for detail; overview for patterns.

title: Why inspect inherited traits?
caption: Recorded example close-up: inherited engine values.
notes: Fecundity shifts the energy needed to reproduce.
Parents transfer energy to their offspring.

title: Fecundity changes the reproduction threshold.
caption: Recorded example close-up: inherited engine values.
notes: Fecundity shifts the energy needed to reproduce.
Parents transfer energy to their offspring.

title: Will this hunter family survive?
caption: Follow descendants across generations.
notes: Gold marks identify the followed family.
Camera-follow tracks its living members.
hint: A family can grow, shrink or disappear.

title: See what this policy actually changes.
caption: Shown: policies for future offspring.
notes: A offspring inherit a lower reproduction threshold.
B offspring inherit more efficient resource feeding.
hint: These policies do not rewrite every living creature.

title: The food web reaches an ending.
caption: Every ending leaves evidence to investigate.
notes: Algae disappear at generation 43; grazers at 90.
Hunters and the followed family are lost at 113.
hint: Follow the losses in the species timeline.

title: Turn the result into another question.
caption: The engine supplies the measured evidence.
notes: Jev selects facts from this run.
Review its proposed next experiment.
hint: Use a turning point to choose the next question.

title: Try more starting resources.
caption: The next choice remains yours.
notes: Review the resource change before seeding.
Keep the original run as the comparison baseline.
hint: Keep the previous run for comparison.

title: Play the changed experiment.
caption: This is a new experiment, not replay.
notes: Observe a new trial under changed conditions.
Fresh adaptive decisions can also differ.
hint: Compare the shapes of the population curves.

title: Did the changed world last longer?
caption: Same seed, fresh adaptive decisions.
notes: Original world: empty at generation 113.
Changed world: empty at generation 158.
hint: This observation does not isolate a resource effect.

title: Keep a world worth investigating.
caption: Keep the experiment you want to revisit.
notes: Save a recognizable world in this browser.
Export a portable backup of its recording.
hint: Browser-local saves do not automatically sync.

title: Choose a world. See what happens.
caption: Play at lifepot.modepot.io
notes: Replay the recorded history without fresh inference.
